note: Both proposals were anchored on lines of the merged fork patch that do not carry the advisory's change: the scheme advisory on the removal of a local req variable, and the JSONP advisory on Context.Scheme, which belongs to the scheme fix. Both rows are held here and were relocated and applied via promote_candidate.py (see relocated_rows). The frozen v4.15.2 tree matches the v4 backport b838391e2ead, not the v5 commit fc410094b2f3.

relocated_rows.reason: The frozen HSTS condition trusts X-Forwarded-Proto from any client when the connection is not TLS, so a plain-HTTP request carrying the header is treated as secure; Context.Scheme has the same unconditional trust and lets direct clients bypass HTTPSRedirect. The fix requires the peer to be a trusted proxy before using forwarded scheme headers and rewrites this condition to config.HSTSMaxAge != 0 && c.Scheme() == "https".

jsonPBlob writes the caller-supplied callback straight into the JavaScript body, so any route forwarding attacker-controlled input as the JSONP callback yields reflected XSS. The fix replaces these two lines with c.writeJSONPHeader, which validates the callback (empty, identifier, or dot-separated identifier path), rejects other values with a 400 wrapping ErrInvalidJSONPCallback before writing, and sets X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

rows.reason: Frozen 109 is only the local req := c.Request() assignment that the fix deletes as part of the refactor. The trust decision is the HSTS condition at frozen 121, which reads X-Forwarded-Proto from any client; the fix changes it to c.Scheme() == "https" and moves the forwarded-header trust behind proxy checks. Relocate to 121.

Context.Scheme is the sink of the other advisory in the same fork merge. The JSONP XSS sink is jsonPBlob, which writes the unvalidated callback into the body; the fix routes it through writeJSONPHeader/isValidJSONPCallback. Relocate to context.go jsonPBlob 501-502.
